root_cause.text: The firmware-controlled key index in b43_rx() is not properly bounds-checked before being used to index the dev->key[] array; the existing B43_WARN_ON does not prevent out-of-bounds access in production builds.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that the key index can exceed the dev->key[] array size (58 entries) and that the existing B43_WARN_ON is non-enforcing. The patch changes the WARN_ON to an enforcing check by adding an early return with `if (B43_WARN_ON(keyidx >= ARRAY_SIZE(dev->key))) goto drop;`, preventing the subsequent out-of-bounds read.

intent_record.intent_summary: Bug fix: after warning on invalid key index, drop the packet to prevent out-of-bounds array access.
intent_record.what: Changed a standalone B43_WARN_ON call to an if statement that jumps to the 'drop' label when the condition is true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, if keyidx is out of bounds, the kernel will still emit a warning but now will also drop the packet instead of continuing to access the key array, preventing a potential out-of-bounds access.

This warning macro does not prevent the subsequent out-of-bounds access in production builds, making the bounds check ineffective and leaving the vulnerability exploitable.
